notes: ACCESS: plain requests/BeautifulSoup direct fetch worked for every URL, no WAF, no proxy needed (matches the prior Home-Decor pass). robots.txt checked first: it disallows only /checkout/, /cart/, /customer/, /lightbox/, /my-favorites/manage/ and /search?, blocks Yandex, and names no Anthropic/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web agent, so no Claude-specific disallow applies. TREE SOURCE: three independent views, all reconciled. (1) The site's own GraphQL getSitemapLinks payload, embedded verbatim in the Apollo SSR blob on https://joybird.com/sitemap/, gives the authoritative parent_id/child category graph (mainCategories + subCategories keyed by parent id). (2) The desktop mega-menu top bar (Living Room | Dining Room | Bedroom | Home Office | Outdoor | Decor | Featured | Sale | Inspiration) confirms the department level and matches the graph's Furniture(id 218) children exactly: Living Room Furniture(601), Bedroom(213), Dining Room(580), Home Office(602), Outdoor(624). (3) The mobile flyout, present in the homepage SSR HTML, gives the product-type groups (Sofas / Chairs / Tables / Bedroom / Storage / Outdoor / Decor) and supplied the few nav-only leaves. sitemap.xml was also enumerated for any category slug missing from all three. QTY METHOD: every listing page is a Next.js App Router page carrying an Algolia InstantSearch (index products_jb4, filter categories:"<slug>") result blob in the SSR HTML. For each leaf I took the rendered '<N> Products' header text (source of truth) and independently the blob's nbHits, and required them to be identical; I also required nbPages == ceil(nbHits/12) with hitsPerPage 12. All 55 URLs (44 leaves + 11 parents) were fetched TWICE, ~25 minutes apart: zero drift, zero disagreement between the two signals, and every page's h1 matched the category requested (no silent parent-serving). Discrimination is proven: the numbers span 0..730 and change per category, so this is not a site-wide constant. No Shopify/products_count-style structured source was used; no tile hrefs were counted. HIERARCHY: parents that are genuine roll-ups were emitted as grouping rows, never as leaves. Verified by reading the SSR hits' own categories[] arrays: /living-room-furniture/ (501), /bedroom/ (76), /dining-room-furniture/ (21), /home-office-furniture/ (12, and it even carries a rug), /outdoor-furniture/ (28), /sofas/ (100), /sectionals/ (103), /chairs/ (90), /ottomans/ (74), /all-storage/ (46) and /all-tables/ (35) each aggregate products that are separately tagged into the child slugs I did record. /all-storage/ and /all-tables/ are cross-department roll-ups (all-storage's page-1 products carry media-consoles, dressers-chests, nightstands, desks, console-and-entry-tables and bookcases-wall-units tags), so their non-storage/non-living-room members are recorded once under Bedroom, Home Office and Tables rather than twice. Sanity note, not used as a source: the six Sofas children happen to sum to exactly 100 = /sofas/'s own total. DROPPED AS ROLL-UPS OR DUPLICATE URLs FOR THE SAME POPULATION: /sofas-and-sectionals/ (203, exactly /sofas/ 100 + /sectionals/ 103); /coffee-and-end-tables/ (37 = coffee 16 + end 21); /end-tables/ (21, h1 'End Tables', identical population to /end-tables-entry-tables/ 21 - products carry both slugs, so only the nav-linked one is emitted); /outdoor-sofas-and-sectionals/ (9, identical to /outdoor-sofas/ 9 and co-tagged on the same products); /shelving/ (1 - its single product is also tagged bookcases-wall-units, i.e. a strict subset of Bookcases & Shelving 4, so emitting it would double-count); /chaises/ (11) and /poufs/ (9) as strict subsets of /daybeds-chaises/ (25) and /ottomans-poufs-and-cubes/ (67); /bundles/ (19 sofa+ottoman and chair+ottoman sets - genuine furniture sets, but 12/12 of its page-1 products are tagged 'ottomans' and 11/12 'ottomans-poufs-and-cubes', so it sits wholly inside the 67 already recorded); /reclining-furniture/ (18, a cross-cutting motion facet whose members are already recorded as Reclining Sofas 6 / Reclining Sectionals 6 / Reclining Chairs 4). DROPPED AS STYLE/SIZE/MATERIAL FACET RE-CUTS of the same catalogue (same convention the prior Home-Decor pass used for /modern/*): /modern/* (26 slugs), /mid-century-furniture/* (138 + 7 children), /small-space-furniture/* (14 + 4 children), /apartment-furniture/ (16), /leather-furniture/, /leather-sofas/ (10), /leather-chairs/ (4), /wood/. Per-brief navigation junk dropped: /all/ (730), /collections/ + its 37 named collection pages, /new-arrivals/ + /new/*, /best-sellers/, /sale/, /featured/, /bipoc-owned/, /bundles/ landing, /lookbooks/, /customer-photos/. DEAD OR NON-LISTING PAGES (HTTP 200 but no product grid, no h1 and no Algolia blob, so no count is obtainable and they were NOT emitted): /modular-sofas/ (11.9 MB pure marketing landing page - it is a mobile-nav item but §3 forbids landing pages, and the site's own category graph gives node id 642 'Modular Sofas' an EMPTY url); /recliners-gliders/ (title just 'Joybird'; replaced by /reclining-chairs/); /daybeds/ (covered by /daybeds-chaises/ 25); /outdoor-sectionals/ (a real category tag - 3 of /outdoor-furniture/'s page-1 products carry it - but every one of them is also tagged outdoor-sofas, so it is a subset of the Outdoor Sofas 9 already recorded). UNLINKED LEGACY ZERO-COUNT SLUGS found in sitemap.xml, all live and all reporting 0, all duplicating a type already represented, so noted here rather than padded into rows: /all-sectionals/, /l-and-u-shaped-sectionals/, /corner-sectional-sleepers/, /table-top-ottomans/, /ottomans-benches/, /credenzas/, /apartment-credenza/, /apartment-desk/. Only /counter-stools/ (0) was emitted from this group, flagged, because it names a furniture type nothing else covers. EXCLUDED PER BRIEF §1: /mattresses/ (0 - bedding, not furniture); /slipcovers/ (19 - furniture covers); /pet-beds/ (1 - pet furniture, filed by the site under Decor); /outdoor-accessories/ (3 - opened it, the products are outdoor PILLOWS, tagged pillows + decoration-accessories); /cushions/, /pillows/, /throws/, /rugs/, /washable-rugs/, /outdoor-rugs/ (textiles); /decoration-accessories/ and its whole subtree - /wall-art/, /wall-decor/, /wallpaper/, /mirrors/, /all-lighting/ + /floor-lamps/ /table-lamps/ /ceiling-lamps/ /pendants/, /vases-and-bowls/, /clocks/, /plants-and-planters/, /tableware/, /glassware/, /serveware/ (lighting, mirrors, wall decor, decor objects, tableware - other workstreams); /fabrics/, /select-fabrics/, /swatches/, /material-swatches/, /samples/ (fabric swatches). Joybird sells no bathroom, kids/nursery or filing-cabinet furniture - none of those slugs exist in sitemap.xml, the mega-menu or the getSitemapLinks graph.
